## Task input
# Avoid confusing tasks with identical names

I created the "speed-up-automated-tests" task from a template again. It then showed all stages complete. This was likely because a task with the same name was already completed. I've since deleted the duplicate and created a new one with a unique name as a workaround.

It should be possible to create tasks with the same name later on and not have it confused with a completed task.

Care should also be taken not to overwrite them. Up to you to decide how, but one idea would be to move completed tasks into a GUID subfolder on completion to avoid collisions.

I now have complete evidence. Here is the diagnosis:

---

## Diagnosis: Stale `.relay/<taskId>/` directory persists after task completion, causing identity collision

### Root cause

When a task completes and its markdown is archived to `llm-tasks/completed/<name>/DONE-<name>.md`, the **`.relay/<name>/` directory is never cleaned**. The stale directory retains the prior run's `status.json` (all stages Done), stage reports, seals, and ledger. There is no code anywhere that deletes or moves `.relay/<taskId>/` on normal completion.

### Concrete on-disk evidence

The `.relay/speed-up-automated-tests/` directory still contains the full prior-run state — proof the cleanup gap is real:

- **`.relay/speed-up-automated-tests/status.json`**: all 12 stages marked "Done" (lines 1–157), with `taskInputHash: "8401049000298d1b52588c23cce9c0ae8f231b6207cf1a1ae864282c8aa28d38"`
- **`.relay/speed-up-automated-tests/stage1-attempt1.report.json`** through `stage10-attempt1.report.json`: full attempt reports with cost/duration data
- **`.relay/speed-up-automated-tests/ledger.md`**, **`manifest.txt`**, **`speed-up-automated-tests.seals`**: all prior-run artifacts

Meanwhile, the markdown was properly archived:
- **`llm-tasks/completed/speed-up-automated-tests/DONE-speed-up-automated-tests.md`** exists
- **`llm-tasks/speed-up-automated-tests/`** does NOT exist (user deleted the duplicate)

### Four independent code paths read the stale state

**1. `RelayTaskWriter.ValidateSlug` (line 58–67) — allows re-creation**
```csharp
var flatPath = Path.Combine(tasksDir, $"{slug}.md");
var nestedDir = Path.Combine(tasksDir, slug);
if (File.Exists(flatPath) || Directory.Exists(nestedDir))
    return $"A task named \"{slug}\" already exists. ...";
```
Only checks `llm-tasks/<slug>.md` and `llm-tasks/<slug>/`. A completed task lives at `llm-tasks/completed/<slug>/DONE-<slug>.md`, so neither path exists. Validation passes and creation succeeds with no warning.

**2. `RelayTaskRepository.AttachRunMetrics` (lines 243–256) — shows stale metrics**
```csharp
private RelayTaskItem AttachRunMetrics(RelayTaskItem task)
{
    var metric = RelayRunHistory.ReadTaskMetric(RootPath, task.Id);
    ...
    return task with
    {
        CostUsd = metric.CostUsd,
        DurationSeconds = metric.DurationSeconds,
        CompletedStageCount = metric.CompletedStageCount,
        ...
    };
}
```
`RelayRunHistory.ReadTaskMetric` (line 13–30 of `RelayRunHistory.cs`) reads `.relay/<taskId>/stage*-attempt*.report.json`. The stale reports produce `CompletedStageCount = 12`, `DurationSeconds`, and `CostUsd` from the prior run, making the new task appear already finished in the queue card.

**3. `RelayQueueController.StagesOneThroughFourAreDone` (lines 10–14) — skips planning**
```csharp
private bool StagesOneThroughFourAreDone(string taskId)
{
    var status = StageStatusRecord.Read(Path.Combine(RootPath, ".relay", taskId));
    return status.Count >= 4 && status.Take(4).All(e => e.Status == "Done");
}
```
Reads the stale `status.json` — all 4 stages Done — so the planning phase is skipped entirely during a drain.

**4. `RelayDriver.LoadResumeState` (lines 23–88) — resumes past all stages**
```csharp
var firstNonDone = priorStatus.FirstOrDefault(e => !StageStatusIsComplete(e.Status));
firstStageToRun = firstNonDone?.Stage ?? (RelayStages.All.Count + 1);
```
When `Resume:true`, reads stale `status.json`. All 12 stages are "Done", so `firstStageToRun = 13`. The stage loop in `RunTaskAsync` (line 69–71) then iterates zero times — everything appears complete. The only guard is `DetectReAddAndArchive` (line 55), but it is gated on `_options.Resume == true` — a fresh non-resume run skips it entirely.

### Why DetectReAddAndArchive doesn't help on fresh runs

`RelayDriver.RunTaskAsync` line 55:
```csharp
var isReAdded = _options.Resume && firstStageToRun > RelayStages.All.Count
    && DetectReAddAndArchive(...);
```
The `_options.Resume` guard means re-add detection is only invoked when explicitly resuming. A normal (non-resume) drain never detects the stale state. And even on resume, if the user didn't modify the task content, the SHA-256 hash matches, so `DetectReAddAndArchive` sees no mismatch and the stale completion state stands.

### No cleanup exists

`TaskCompletionArchive.RetireAsync` (line 20–23) only does:
```csharp
try { Execution.FlaggedWorkStore.Delete(taskDirectory); } catch { /* best-effort */ }
```
`FlaggedWorkStore.Delete` removes only flagged-work snapshots — it does NOT delete `status.json`, stage reports, seals, or ledger. `ExecuteCommitStageAsync` calls `FlaggedWorkStore.Delete` again (line 281) but never removes the `.relay/<taskId>/` directory itself.

The only code that moves `.relay/<taskId>/` is `ArchivePriorRunState` (ReAdd.cs line 108), which only fires on resume re-add with content mismatch — never on normal completion.

### Reproduction

1. Create task "speed-up-automated-tests", run through all 12 stages to completion. Task markdown moves to `llm-tasks/completed/speed-up-automated-tests/DONE-speed-up-automated-tests.md`. `.relay/speed-up-automated-tests/status.json` shows all Done.
2. Create a new task with the identical title/slug "speed-up-automated-tests". `ValidateSlug` passes because `llm-tasks/speed-up-automated-tests/` doesn't exist (it was moved to `completed/`).
3. Queue card shows `CompletedStageCount: 12`, cost, and duration from the prior run (via `AttachRunMetrics` → `RelayRunHistory.ReadTaskMetric`).
4. On drain, `StagesOneThroughFourAreDone` returns `true` → planning skipped.
5. If not in resume mode, stages 5+ may run from scratch (or the pipeline finds all stages Done and shows "complete").
